clue.text: Two horsepower mode of transport

parts.note: read literally, a vehicle drawn by a couple of actual horses rather than a car with a tiny engine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Two horsepower' sounds like a feeble engine rating, but here it means two real horses pulling a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach drawn by a matched couple of horses is the classic horse-drawn vehicle of that name.

clue.text: Struggle — hold on!

explanation.surface: A cry of encouragement to someone wrestling: keep holding!
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with something is to struggle with it, and getting a grip is literally taking hold.

clue.text: Dress fittings more expensive

parts.note: a ship's rig is its fittings of masts and sails
prices that are up have risen, so they are more expensive

explanation.surface: Clothing accessories are going up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit someone out in clothes or costume is to deck them out, a phrasal verb for dressing.

clue.text: Laid on thick by artist

parts.note: describes the painting technique in which pigment is applied heavily enough to stand out from the canvas

explanation.definitionFit: The term names the painting technique of applying paint in thick, textured layers.

clue.text: Grand saint in virtuous environment who is spiritual

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: the saint is placed in the word for virtuous, inside it

parts.note: virtuous means holy

explanation.surface: A great saint surrounded by goodness is someone very spiritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is a link here, reinforcing that HOLY surrounds ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectral or otherworldly is spiritual in the sense of belonging to the spirit world.

clue.text: An archdeacon had good start before editor retaliated

indicators.note: the previous pieces come before the next one in the answer

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: the start of the word good is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchman got off to a good start and then got his revenge on the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To take revenge for a wrong is to strike back, which is to retaliate.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the Parisian duo

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A French couple in a state of despondency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals French: DES is the French for 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Total loss of hope is the meaning of the word, a synonym of hopelessness.

clue.text: Person renouncing Jack, one who is saying no

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is also a sailor
one who negates, denies or says no, is a negator

explanation.surface: A man gives up Jack, the fellow who always refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnegation is self-denial or renunciation, so this person is someone who gives things up.

clue.text: It is as far as trainees can go!

definitions.text: It is as far as trainees can go!

parts.words: It is as far as trainees can go!
parts.note: trainees here are passengers on a train, and the end of the line is where they must stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'trainees' suggests apprentices with limits on progress, but read it as people on trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The final station on a line is the farthest point a train passenger can reach.

clue.text: Extremely large ring on loudhailer

parts.note: mega is slang for extremely large or great
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A huge ring is placed on a loudhailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped device for amplifying the voice is a synonym of loudhailer.

clue.text: Scotsman is returning to the mount

indicators.note: the pieces are read backwards, as if coming back the way they came

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot is going back to the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses both IAN and IS together, giving SI + NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments is the mount meant.

clue.text: Oriental heard Pete's prepared and arranged it ready for printing

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken, so its spelling follows the sound

parts.note: Thai means from Thailand, an Oriental country

indicators.note: prepared means worked up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its s, as written

explanation.surface: An Asian man listened as Pete got the copy ready for the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns THAI into its sound, TY; 'prepared' rearranges PETES into PESET.
explanation.definitionFit: To set type is to arrange the letters for a press, ready for printing.

clue.text: Unnatural gas in warm reflected light in the city

indicators.note: the shuffled gas is put in the word for light, inside it

parts.note: a glow is a warm, soft light

indicators.note: unnatural signals the letters of gas are put in a new, unnatural order

explanation.surface: Strange gases in a warm glow over the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm reflected light' is one phrase for a soft glow, not separate pieces. Glasgow is Scotland's largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, so it fits the definition as a specific example.

clue.text: Strong alkaline solution found in the west Midlands

explanation.surface: A caustic liquid discovered in the industrial heart of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Lye is a small town near Stourbridge in the West Midlands, an English region around Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic potash or soda dissolved in water is the cleaning solution; the same name belongs to a Black Country town near Stourbridge.

clue.text: George, young leader, holds record on the study of the earth

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the record inside them
the leader of young is its first letter

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: George, a young leader, keeps a record of earth science.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of rocks and the earth's structure is an exact synonym of earth science.

clue.text: Leader of ensemble left Rochester replaced by a band

indicators.note: by means alongside, so the a is set beside the rearranged letters
re-placed, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
the leader has left, departing from the word Rochester
the leader of ensemble is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The ensemble's leader quit Rochester and was replaced by a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes E from ROCHESTER, leaving ROCHSTER, which 'replaced' rearranges into ORCHESTR before A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A large body of musicians playing together is a band in the broad sense.

clue.text: Good Greek character's a beast!

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A good Greek character turns out to be a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest is an African animal, so it is an example of a beast.

clue.text: Door collapsed by your old lady

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other
a collapsed door has fallen apart, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Your old woman knocked the door down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges DOOR into DORO. 'old lady' looks like the definition, but 'old' goes with 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, so this is an example of a lady.

clue.text: Have to concede this goal

explanation.surface: A defender must give away this goal.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal is one a player scores against their own side, so it is conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to have; to admit is to concede, and an own goal is one a side concedes to itself.

clue.text: Nightmare in island disregarding a busy centre

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so the a is left out

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

indicators.note: the centre of busy is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A bad dream about an island that has no busy town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an evil spirit thought to weigh on sleepers, hence a bad dream or nightmare.

clue.text: Benjamin and I accepted girl, one coming from se Asia

indicators.note: accepted means took in, so the girl goes inside

parts.note: Ben is short for Benjamin
gal is a colloquial word for girl

explanation.surface: Benjamin and I took in a girl from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Bengal, the region of the Indian subcontinent, is a person from that part of Asia.

clue.text: Treacherous person set about royal scribe

indicators.note: about means around, so set goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
royal gives R
to pen is to write, as a scribe does

explanation.surface: A traitor sets about the king's scribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a byword for someone sly and treacherous, as in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Some of the women for certain had drive

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain women showed determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'had drive' as the definition, but a verb meaning compel cannot stand for 'had drive'; 'drive' alone is the definition and 'had' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to act is to compel them, which is to impose or enforce it.

clue.text: Sees raw material that is extremely ugly

parts.note: to eye something is to see it
ore is the raw material from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the raw material is hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly thing that offends the view is something very ugly.

clue.text: Completely unimaginative

parts.note: describes writing that contains nothing invented, only the truth

explanation.definitionFit: Something based purely on truth, with nothing invented, contains no imagination at all.

clue.text: See fenland community

explanation.surface: Look at a small town in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in the Cambridgeshire Fens (flat drained marshland in eastern England), has a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's diocese, and a small city in the Cambridgeshire marshlands.

clue.text: Backer?

parts.note: read as 'more to the back', the comparative of the word for a ship's rear end

explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the back of a ship, so something further aft is jokingly more back.

clue.text: Shout out demand for alimony

parts.note: alimony is paid to a former spouse, an ex
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out a demand for maintenance money.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'demand for alimony' is a pun: it describes what a former spouse makes, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly is to shout, a synonym.

clue.text: Farewell notice that is universal

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
i.e. is short for id est, that is
U is the British film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A notice of goodbye that applies to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word for goodbye is a synonym of farewell.

clue.text: Having arrived, drawing back within

parts.note: a train that is in has arrived

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round, read from the end

parts.note: drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: Once arrived, someone pulls back inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin prefix means inside, as in intravenous, a synonym of within.

clue.text: Notice Lou's development in which delivery is important

indicators.note: development means the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the name without its possessive s

explanation.surface: Lou develops an art where speaking clearly matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of clear speech is all about how words are spoken, which is delivery.

clue.text: Engaged in daydreaming and having a misty outlook

explanation.surface: A dreamy person with a foggy view of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lost in fantasy, and literally describes peering out from within fog.
